## Summary
Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.
One Important defect remains open: the invite flow still accepts 8-character passwords, so the twelve-character policy described in this pull request can be bypassed. This review traced every `MIN_PASSWORD_LENGTH` definition and every `accepts_password` caller and test in the repository, and found that `app/invite.py` still uses the old minimum. The updated parametrizations in `tests/test_reset.py:6` and `tests/test_signup.py:6` include 11 and 12, so they cover both sides of the new boundary for those two modules.

## Changes
The pull request raises `MIN_PASSWORD_LENGTH` from 8 to 12 in `app/reset.py` and `app/signup.py` and changes their boundary tests to check 0, 8, 11, 12 and 13. It also adds a one-line `review.txt` file.

## Critical
(none)

## Important
- app/signup.py:1 — correctness — Raise the invite flow's minimum password length to 12 — The pull request raises the minimum only in signup and reset, so `app/invite.py:1` still has `MIN_PASSWORD_LENGTH = 8`. As a result, `app.invite.accepts_password("x" * 9)` returns `True`. The PR body says "This raises the minimum in the password validators" and says the policy "now requires passwords of at least twelve characters". `app/invite.py:4-5` is the same validator, and `tests/test_invite.py:6-8` still asserts `length >= 8`. — A user who sets a password through an invite can still choose an 8- to 11-character password, which bypasses the security policy this change is meant to enforce. — Fix: Set `MIN_PASSWORD_LENGTH = 12` in `app/invite.py:1`, and change `tests/test_invite.py:6-8` to the same `[0, 8, 11, 12, 13]` / `length >= 12` form used in the other two test files.
